Q888658.label: José Agripino Barnet
Q888658.summary: José Agripino Barnet y Vinageras was a Cuban politician and diplomat who served as interim President of Cuba from December 11, 1935 to May 20, 1936.

Q562002.label: Salvador Jorge Blanco
Q562002.summary: José Salvador Omar Jorge Blanco was a Dominican politician, lawyer and writer who served as the 48th president of the Dominican Republic from 1982 to 1986. He was a Senator running for the PRD party. He started his political career as a Committee Secretary for the Unión Cívica de Santiago in 1963 and joined the PRD in 1964.

Q17515858.label: Modern Revolutionary Party
Q17515858.desc: political party in the Dominican Republic
Q17515858.summary: The Modern Revolutionary Party is a political party in the Dominican Republic. It emerged after a division within the Dominican Revolutionary Party (PRD). It was recognized on 9 September 2014. The PRM is the legal heir of the Dominican Social Alliance.

Q1278802.label: Vlatko Pavletić
Q1278802.summary: Vlatko Pavletić was a Croatian politician, university professor, literary critic and essayist who served as acting President of Croatia from 1999 to 2000, as well as he served as Speaker of the Croatian Parliament from 1995 to 2000.

Q2053970.summary: General elections were held in Bosnia and Herzegovina on 1 October 2006. They decided the makeup of Bosnia and Herzegovina's Presidency as well as national, entity, and cantonal governments.

Q1892690.label: 2001 Moldovan parliamentary election
Q1892690.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Moldova on 25 February 2001. The result was a victory for the Party of Communists of the Republic of Moldova (PCRM), which won 71 of the 101 seats.

Q494930.label: Matthew Ridgway
Q494930.summary: Matthew Bunker Ridgway was a senior officer in the United States Army, who served as Supreme Allied Commander Europe (1952–1953) and the 19th Chief of Staff of the United States Army (1953–1955). Although he saw no combat service in World War I, he was intensively involved in World War II, where he was the first Commanding General (CG) of the 82nd Airborne Division, leading it in action in Sicily, Italy and Normandy, before taking command of the newly formed XVIII Airborne Corps in August 1944.

Q1144146.label: Japan Socialist Party
Q1144146.summary: The Japan Socialist Party was a major socialist, progressive, and left-wing political party in Japan. Established in 1945, the party was the primary representative of the Japanese left and main opponent of the right-wing Liberal Democratic Party for most of its existence.

Q494418.label: Rangoon bombing
Q494418.desc: assassination attempt against Chun Doo-hwan, the fifth president of South Korea, in 1983
Q494418.summary: The Rangoon bombing of 9 October 1983 was an assassination attempt orchestrated by North Korea against Chun Doo-hwan, the fifth president of South Korea, in Rangoon, Burma. Although Chun survived, 21 people died in the attack and 46 were injured.

Q214866.label: Great Hanshin Earthquake
Q214866.summary: The Kobe earthquake, also known as the Great Hanshin Earthquake , occurred on January 17, 1995, at 05:46:53 JST in the southern part of Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan, including the region of Hanshin. It measured 6.9 on the moment magnitude scale and had a maximum intensity of 7 on the JMA Seismic Intensity Scale. The tremors lasted for approximately 20 seconds.

Q814930.label: Treaty of Accession 2003
Q814930.summary: The Treaty of Accession 2003 was the agreement between the member states of the European Union and ten countries, concerning these countries' accession into the EU. At the same time it changed a number of points which were originally laid down in the Treaty of Nice.

mentions.c: Greece: Treaty signed: Treaty of Accession 2003

Q19950418.label: Japanese occupation of Thailand
Q19950418.summary: Thailand officially adopted a neutral position during World War II until the five hour-long Japanese invasion of Thailand on 8 December 1941, which led to an armistice and military alliance treaty between Thailand and the Empire of Japan in mid-December 1941. At the start of the Pacific War, the Japanese Empire pressured the Thai government to allow the passage of Japanese troops to invade British-held Malaya and Burma. After the invasion, the Thai government was placed under Plaek Phibunsongkhram.

Q29561682.label: Rhineland Offensive
Q29561682.desc: series of allied offensive operations by 21st Army Group commanded by Bernard Montgomery from 8 February 1945 to 25 March 1945
Q29561682.img: Churchill tanks of 107th Regiment RAC (King's Own), 34th Tank Brigade, at the start of the Reichswald battle in Germany, 9 February 1945. B14422.jpg
Q29561682.summary: The Rhineland Offensive was a series of allied offensive operations by 21st Army Group commanded by Bernard Montgomery from 8 February 1945 to 25 March 1945, at the end of the Second World War. The operations were aimed at occupying the Rhineland and securing a passage over the Rhine river.

Q486226.label: Phong Nhi and Phong Nhat massacre
Q486226.desc: 1968 killing of Vietnamese villagers reportedly by South Korean marines
Q486226.wiki: Phong Nhị and Phong Nhất massacre
Q486226.summary: The Phong Nhị and Phong Nhất massacre was a massacre of unarmed civilians in the villages of Phong Nhị and Phong Nhất, Điện Bàn District of Quảng Nam Province in South Vietnam reported to have been conducted by the 2nd Marine Brigade of the Republic of Korea Marines (ROKMC) during the Vietnam War on 12 February 1968.

Q4871506.label: Battle of Kushtia
Q4871506.desc: battle of the Bangladesh Liberation War
Q4871506.summary: The Battle of Kushtia was a battle between the Bengali guerrillas including policemen against the Pakistan Army in March and April 1971, The battle was fought by the Mukti Fauj and the 27th Baluch Regiment of the Pakistan Army.

Q2026322.label: Operation Rock Avalanche
Q2026322.summary: Operation Rock Avalanche was a six-day, US-led offensive from 19 to 25 October 2007, with the purpose of hunting Taliban fighters in the Korengal Valley of Afghanistan. The mission also aimed to establish a peace with the local populace so that a road could be safely built through the area by the Afghan government. Over the course of the operation, a series of running battles occurred with members of the Taliban, as well as with local tribesmen. U.S. Army Paratrooper Salvatore Giunta would be awarded the Medal of Honor for his actions during combat between U.S. forces and local Afghans.

Q7097682.label: Operation Valiant Guardian
Q7097682.summary: Operation Valiant Guardian began in 2007 and was part of the Iraq War.

Q39899474.label: Deir ez-Zor campaign (2017–2019)
Q39899474.desc: military operation by Syrian Democratic Forces during the Syrian Civil War
Q39899474.summary: The Deir ez-Zor campaign, codenamed the al-Jazeera Storm campaign, was a military operation launched by the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) against the Islamic State (IS) in Syria's Deir ez-Zor Governorate in 2017 during the Syrian Civil War with the goal of capturing territory in eastern Syria, particularly east and north of the Euphrates river.

Q42834.label: Western Roman Empire
Q42834.desc: independently administered western provinces of the Roman Empire
Q42834.summary: In modern historiography, the Western Roman Empire was the Roman Empire's western provinces collectively during any period in which they were administered separately from the eastern provinces by a separate, independent imperial court. Particularly from AD 395 to 476, there were separate, coequal courts dividing the governance of the empire into western and eastern provinces with a distinct imperial succession in the separate courts.

Q2707282.label: Sammarinese Socialist Party
Q2707282.summary: The Sammarinese Socialist Party was a socialist and, later, social-democratic political party in San Marino. Its Italian counterpart was the Italian Socialist Party and its international affiliation was with the Socialist International.

Q11168082.label: cultural conservatism
Q11168082.desc: conservative ideology advocating for the preservation of cultural traditions
Q11168082.summary: Cultural conservatism is described as the protection of the cultural heritage of a nation state, or of a culture not defined by state boundaries. It is sometimes associated with criticism of multiculturalism, and anti-immigration sentiment. Because their cultural preservationist objectives are in conflict with those of anti-racists, cultural conservatives are often accused of racism.

Q189266.label: Eastern Front
aliases: Eastern Front of World War II
Q189266.img: Bundesarchiv Bild 146-1981-149-34A, Russland, Herausziehen eines Autos.jpg
Q189266.summary: The Eastern Front, also known as the Great Patriotic War, or the German–Soviet War, was a theatre of World War II fought between the European Axis powers and Allies, including the Soviet Union (USSR) and Poland. It encompassed Central Europe, Eastern Europe, Northeast Europe (Baltics), and Southeast Europe (Balkans), and lasted from 22 June 1941 to 9 May 1945. Of the estimated 70–85 million deaths attributed to the war, around 30 million occurred on the Eastern Front, including 9 million children.

Q185682.label: French Indochina
Q185682.img: Sa Majesté Bao-Daï fit le pèlerinage aux Tombeaux des ancêtres de la Dynastie à Thanh-Hóa, 1932.jpg
Q185682.summary: French Indochina, officially known as the Indochinese Union and after 1941 as the Indochinese Federation, was a group of French-dependent territories in Southeast Asia from 1887 to 1954. It was initially a federation of French colonies (1887–1949), later a confederation of French associated states (1949–1954). It comprised Cambodia, Laos, Guangzhouwan (1898–1945), Cochinchina, and Vietnamese regions of Tonkin and Annam. It was established in 1887 and was dissolved in 1954. In 1949, Vietnam was reunited and it regained Cochinchina. Its capitals were Hanoi (1902–1945) and Saigon.
